title: A Simple Point in the Middle
paragraphs: It is a common trait among scholars - of the past as well as the present -- who have penned commentaries on the old Tamiḻ words and phrases to overlook the comprehension potential of the readers.

Instead of providing simple explanations, they prefer to tread on rough terrain, by being pedantic like classical musicians, who flaunt all the finer nuances of music in a concert, to be appreciated by only a hundred people among multitudes of laymen.
To be precise, how many presons know as to what exactly tiṇai means?
Tiṇai is the term related to aspects of behaviour, land division and classes of beings. While uyartiṇai refers to human beings, akṟiṇai denotes things non-human.

Akattiṇai signifies the love career of the hero and the heroine through the phases of union, separation, patient waiting, sulking, etc., and deals with the pre-marital and marital relations of these two, with akam, the heart, standing at the base. There is also the unrequited love and abnormal sexual passion.

Aintiṇai is the fivefold love career of the hero and the heroine -- kuṟiñci (the union of the lovers), pālai (separation), marutam (feigned love quarrels), mullai (patient waiting of the heroine), and neytal (the lamentation in separation).
Even as union, separation, etc., may occur in all classes of land, we need to look at tiṇai as a place or land of occurrence of an event of love.

Puṟattiṇai is the parallel, the counterpoint of Akattiṇai. While Akam is the intimacy of love behaviour and conjugal life between a man and a woman, Puṟam signifies aspects of life in the society at large such as war, governance, learning, friendship, etc. The Puṟam events, like the Akam ones, are both land-specific and universal.
This simple explanation would be useful in understanding the issues of akam and puṟam life in their complexities - the breeze, the storm, the tremors of the earth in the life of men and women.
